subject: Top-up amendment & co-term path for Orchid Labs

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Collins <emma@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Top-up amendment & co-term path for Orchid Labs

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, Orchid is looking to add a short-term top-up to handle a seasonal surge and align the expanded capacity with your existing annual renewal in November. I sketched two practical paths below so procurement can pick the one that works best operationally: 

Option A — Top-up (pay-as-you-go uplift) + next renewal annualize
- Immediate: Add 300k token units for the remainder of Q3 at a 15% uplift rate (billed monthly).
- Renewal impact: At November renewal, we convert top-up usage into a 12-month committed bucket and apply a blended discount that accounts for the uplift usage.
- Pros: Fast to approve, minimal legal work; no contract amendment needed now.

Option B — Mid-contract amendment (co-term & true-up)
- Immediate: Amend current order with a short addendum for the 300k units, co-term to November, prorate on a daily basis.
- Renewal impact: Co-termed capacity rolls into renewal as committed units with a pre-agreed discount schedule.
- Pros: Cleaner billing alignment at renewal; better predictability for Orchid.

Proposed commercial levers we can use:
- Tiered discounts by uplift band (15% @ up to 500k; 18% for 500–1M; 22% >1M)
- Option for limited-time early-payment credit (1% off if PO & payment received within 15 days)

I attached a short term sheet that shows the math and suggested proration language. If procurement prefers Option B we can prepare the amendment template and route it through legal — otherwise Option A gets you capacity today and we can reconcile at renewal.

Next steps: can procurement confirm preferred path and whether a PO is required up front? I can loop in Legal/Finance as needed.

—Jordan

2) We typically require EOM invoicing and a PO to process payment. Can Redwood support EOM invoices and accept a net-30 PO for the amended amount?

Emma / Procurement —

Quick answers and a clean suggested approach so Legal + Procurement have what they need.

1) Discount banding: For Orchid we recommend evaluating uplift bands against the incremental top-up only (not aggregating with existing committed usage). Rationale: simplifies the amendment and avoids re-pricing current committed units mid-term. If you want to aggregate for a deeper discount, we can model a blended rate at renewal but that requires a mutual commitment in the amendment.

2) Billing: Redwood can issue EOM invoices and accept a net-30 PO. For Option B we'll add explicit invoicing cadence in the addendum (invoice at month-end for the prior month of uplift usage; payment terms net-30).

Suggested amendment highlights (text to drop in):
- Effective date: date of signed addendum
- Capacity: +300,000 token units (top-up)
- Proration: daily proration from effective date to co-term date (November 30, 2026)
- Discount: 15% off list for the top-up band (applies to top-up consumption during the term)
- Billing: EOM invoicing; net-30; PO accepted
- Renewal: On co-term, both parties will convert top-up consumption into a committed bucket with a blended discount to be reflected on the renewal quote

I've attached a one-page amendment sketch and a short procurement Q&A that should speed review. If Procurement sends their template I'll map our language to it and return a tracked addendum.

Deal reference: RDW-8372 — I'll also update HubSpot with the amendment stage.

Thanks — Ben

Procurement here. We appreciate the clarity. We can proceed with Option B on the following conditions:
